paragraphs: Pinhas, brother of Shmuel the priest, Megillah 22, end of a; and his brother-in-law, Sanhedrin 28b. He asked Shmuel, and Shmuel applied to him ‘the lame plundered spoil’ [Heilprin prints פנחם בזזו בז; Bekhorot and Isaiah read פסחים בזזו בז], because he knew one halakhah; Arakhin (it should read Bekhorot 39a). Rashi explains that it is inconceivable for lame men to plunder; that is, you are not sharp-witted. On cutting nails during the festival’s intermediate days: Mar Shmuel went to him when he was in mourning and saw that his nails were long. He asked, ‘Why have you not cut them?’ He replied, ‘Had it happened to you, would you have treated it so lightly?’ It was like an inadvertent utterance, and the misfortune befell Mar Shmuel; Mo'ed Katan 18a. It thus appears that Pinhas was a son of Abba bar Abba, Shmuel's father; this needs examination.
